No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Stakeholders Call for Constructive Youth Engagement in Nigeria’s Governance by LEADERSHIP News 1 minute ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Nigerian entrepreneur and Founder of Silver Group, Suleiman Abdulsalam, has called for greater youth participation in Nigeria’s governance, emphasising the importance of constructive engagement, public accountability and practical solutions to the country’s development challenges.
Abdulsalam maintains that young Nigerians have a significant role to play in shaping the nation’s future by engaging with public institutions, contributing innovative ideas and participating in policy discussions that affect their social and economic prospects.
He argues that youth inclusion should extend beyond political representation to encompass economic planning, entrepreneurship, technical development and public policy formulation. According to this perspective, creating meaningful opportunities for young people to contribute their expertise and ideas is essential to harnessing their potential for national progress.
The Silver Group founder also highlights the need to balance public accountability with respect for democratic institutions. He maintains that sustainable development requires constructive dialogue and collaboration among government institutions, the private sector and citizens.
His position underscores the importance of moving beyond criticism to practical engagement, with young Nigerians encouraged to propose workable solutions, support responsible governance and contribute to addressing challenges affecting communities and the wider economy.
With Nigeria’s youthful population representing a significant source of talent, innovation and entrepreneurial capacity, Abdulsalam’s perspective places emphasis on creating an environment where young people can participate meaningfully in decisions that shape the country’s development trajectory.
His call reflects a broader conversation about the role of young Nigerians in strengthening democratic participation, improving institutional accountability and supporting economic resilience.
Ultimately, Abdulsalam’s position is that national development requires a shared commitment from both leaders and citizens. By combining constructive civic engagement with innovation, enterprise and practical problem-solving, young Nigerians can contribute to building a more inclusive and economically resilient country.
